transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-12 11:00 PT | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (HaloTech CTO), Sofia Park (HaloTech Sr ML Eng), Derek Huang (HaloTech Head of Platform)

Summary:
Quick discovery to validate time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectations for a PLG onramp, discuss free credit sizing and what triggers Dedicated or Private evaluation, gather security/stakeholder needs, agree next steps for a short benchmark and follow-up deep-dive on VPC options.

Topics (auto-gen):
- Quickstart / credits / TTFT
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
- Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO
- Pilot benchmarks and success criteria
- Next steps and owners

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Rivera: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out the time. Um, quick intro — I'm Alex, AE on the account, and with me is Priya our SE who'll handle the tech bits.
[00:10] Marcus Lee: Hey Alex, thanks. Marcus here. We have Sofia and Derek on the line. We're exploring how fast we can put something in front of product for a small pilot.
[00:18] Sofia Park: Hi, yeah trying to get to a demo inside our app within a couple weeks if possible.
[00:22] Priya Desai: Awesome. Quick question — when you say demo inside the app, is that behind auth for internal users or public facing?
[00:28] Derek Huang: Internal first. We want to make sure there's no PHI leakage and that logs don't get out to a third party.
[00:34] Alex Rivera: Totally got it. That's a common path. The PLG/self-serve flow we usually recommend is: we give you trial credits, set up a sandbox API key, and you can be making calls in under an hour. The TTFT for a basic text generation flow is usually under 1 hour for engineering teams — from sign up to first valid tokens.
[00:53] Marcus Lee: Under an hour, okay. What's the caveat there — like model choice, sequence lengths?
[00:59] Priya Desai: Yeah, sequence length and the model family matter. For a quick pilot we'd suggest a smaller open model variant we have in the catalog that balances cost and latency. If you want lower latency at scale you can move to our Redwood Dedicated pools or even private VPC if you need total data isolation.
[01:15] Sofia Park: For the pilot we expect short prompts, single-turn Q/A, maybe embeddings for search. QPS low to start (around 10-20 rps peak).
[01:23] Alex Rivera: Perfect. For that footprint hosted is usually the fastest and most cost effective. We'll give 30k tokens worth of credits so you can exercise the flow, and if you like it we can expand.
[01:33] Derek Huang: How do you handle data retention and logs? We need audit logs and KMS for keys.
[01:38] Priya Desai: We support customer-managed keys via KMS for Private deployments, and in Hosted we have envelope encryption and can integrate with enterprise KMS in Dedicated/private setups. Audit logs and request traces are available in the Console; we can export them to your SIEM. I'll follow up with the SOC2 and audit guide.
[01:54] Marcus Lee: Cool. Also curious about SSO for the console and RBAC for keys.
[01:59] Alex Rivera: Yes SSO (SAML/SCIM) and RBAC are part of our enterprise features. For the PLG quickstart you can use a lightweight team invite flow, but when you're ready we'll wire up SAML and enforced RBAC.
[02:11] Sofia Park: Are there hard rate limits during the trial? We want to stress the thing a bit.
[02:15] Priya Desai: Trial keys have soft quotas to prevent accidental abuse but we can bump them for tests — just ask. For dedicated you get reserved throughput and custom autoscaling.
[02:24] Alex Rivera: Also worth mentioning function calling and streaming support if you're doing chat-like interfaces. The quickstart covers streaming examples in the SDK.
[02:32] Marcus Lee: Sounds good. Can you do a quick sketch of the decision triggers for Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private?
[02:38] Priya Desai: Sure. Hosted is the default for speed and cost-efficiency during prototyping. Dedicated is when you need predictable, SLA-backed throughput (e.g., sustained high QPS) or stricter tenancy isolation. Private/VPC is for regulatory/data residency or when you require customer-managed KMS and private control plane. Another trigger is latency SLOs — if you need sub-50ms tail latency at scale we might change routing, kernel selection, or move to dedicated hardware.
[03:05] Derek Huang: Sub-50ms seems optimistic for our use case but we should measure.
[03:09] Priya Desai: Right, that's why we'll run a micro-benchmark. We'll ask for a sample trace and some representative payloads. Then we can pick a model variant and run a 48-hour benchmark to show latency and per-token cost.
[03:22] Marcus Lee: Ok that benchmark would be helpful to justify costs to the execs.
[03:26] Alex Rivera: Absolutely. We'll also include a simple cost breakdown — tokens per request, average tokens per session, and estimated monthly spend at your projected QPS.
[03:35] Sofia Park: One more thing: can we test embeddings locally? We have a vector store pipeline and want to see embedding consistency and throughput.
[03:41] Priya Desai: Yes, embeddings are fully supported in the hosted API. For heavy embedding workloads you might consider dedicated pools to reduce latency and cost. There's also recommendations for quantized model variants in the Optimize docs — we sometimes call it 'Red Wood Optimize' in internal notes — sorry, internal slip, it's Redwood Optimize.
[03:59] (laugh)
[04:02] Marcus Lee: No worries. On compliance, would Dedicated still send any user text to Redwood logs? We need a guarantee it never leaves a private environment.
[04:10] Priya Desai: With Private deployment in your VPC + customer-managed keys, logs can be kept in your environment; control plane interactions are minimal and we can disable certain telemetry. We'll include the exact wording in the security pack.
[04:22] Derek Huang: Good. Network topology — do you require peering or can we use private endpoints?
[04:27] Priya Desai: Both options. We support VPC peering or PrivateLink-style endpoints depending on cloud. We'll walk through with your infra team.
[04:35] Sofia Park: About the SDKs — we use Python and Node. Are both well supported?
[04:39] Alex Rivera: Yes strong SDKs for Python, Node, and a curl REST path. Examples in the quickstart show how to stream and do function calling.
[04:48] Marcus Lee: For the trial, can we get programmatic keys and rotate them?
[04:52] Alex Rivera: Yes, programmatic keys with rotation and scoped keys are part of the flow. We'll show you how to scope a key to dev-only endpoints.
[04:59] [05:00] Sofia Park: Could you talk licensing/pricing a little — like per-token vs committed?
[05:03] Alex Rivera: Hosted is usage-based per token; Dedicated is committed capacity (monthly/yearly) with overage rules; Private has a platform fee plus support tier. We'll send a short pricing matrix. For the trial we'll give the credits so you can exercise the real billing meter.
[05:18] Marcus Lee: Would love to see a sample billing estimate for our projected 20rps profile, with and without caching/batching.
[05:25] Priya Desai: We'll include that in the benchmark deliverable — show per-request token burn, batching gains, and caching impact.
[05:31] Derek Huang: On caching — do you support prefix or KV cache? We need to avoid double compute for repeated context.
[05:36] Priya Desai: We support KV cache and prefix caching in the serving runtime; it's configurable per-route.
[05:41] Marcus Lee: Great. Any blockers you foresee for a 2-week onramp?
[05:45] Alex Rivera: Not really. Typical blockers are internal procurement or SOC2 sign-off for data-sensitive apps. But for an internal-only pilot you can often start on hosted with trial keys while we engage security.
[05:57] Sofia Park: Timeline-wise, if we get credits tomorrow we can have a dev branch calling in 48 hours.
[06:02] Alex Rivera: Perfect. We'll aim to provision credits and the quickstart link by tomorrow. Priya will run the bench and we'll reconvene after results.
[06:11] Marcus Lee: Cool. Anything else from your side?
[06:14] Derek Huang: Can you include a short architecture note for the Private deployment so we can show infra?
[06:19] Priya Desai: Yes, I'll attach an infra sketch and outline the peering/private endpoint options.
[06:24] Alex Rivera: Great. Let's recap with concrete next steps.
[06:28] (recap)
[06:30] Alex Rivera: Action items: Alex to provision 30k credits and send quickstart link; Priya to schedule 48h micro-benchmark and grab sample payloads; Marcus to share request traces and expected QPS; Priya to send SOC2 & KMS guide. We'll schedule the 60-minute VPC deep-dive for next week.
[06:49] Sofia Park: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the bench.
[06:52] Alex Rivera: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links and dates.

End of transcript.
